newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil cuts tax on foreign loans for re-lending.
newsitem.headline: Brazil cuts tax on foreign loans for re-lending.

text.p: Brazil has cut a tax charged on banks borrowing abroad for re-lending to the domestic market, dovetailing with the recent launch of the country's global bond offer, Central Bank director Gustavo Franco said.
A Central Bank resolution has reduced the rate of Financial Operations Tax (IOF) banks have to pay on loans secured overseas to three percent from a previous five for three-year loans.

Loans of between three and four years will pay two percent, down from four, while loans of between four and five years will pay one percent, down from two. Loans of over five years are exempt from the tax.
Another change exempted from IOF all loans secured by banks overseas for re-lending to the real estate sector.
The tax cut came as a part of a wider trend in Brazil to cut the cost of borrowing.
"Having done the global (bond launch) to lower Brazil's benchmark, we need to go out there and use it," Franco told reporters.

Franco said one of the aims of Brazil's $750 million, five-year global bond, which was launched on Monday, was to reduce the cost of Brazilian borrowing. The bond was placed at a spread lower than that of any previous large Brazilian government issue.
Another Central Bank official said the move was part of an ongoing plan to gradually reduce IOF on foreign borrowing for re-lending.
